tldr: Monday delivered the rebound the weekend only promised: Nvidia's board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO (reportedly under Trump pressure, 11 days after his Nov 12 resignation), driving NVDA +31-34% -- the largest single-day market-cap gain on record (~$900bn) -- and lifting the S&P 500 +4.73% to 7237.17, Nasdaq +6.51%, VIX -25.8% to 26.62, the broadest US rally since April 2025. Gold/silver/miners V-shaped the same way (SLV +5.25%, GDX +6.43%), confirming Friday's crash was margin-driven liquidation rather than a change in physical fundamentals.

But credit and rates did not confirm the bounce: Dec 9 Fed-hike odds actually ROSE Monday to ~97-98% even as stocks rallied, HY OAS stayed pinned near 352bp with CCC spreads near cycle-wide levels (~1,350bp+), and Nvidia's SEC accounting-practices probe into revenue-geography reporting remains open, unresolved by the CEO swap. Sell-side voices (Capital Economics, Swissquote) are explicitly calling Monday a dead-cat bounce, not a turn.

Asia diverged sharply from the US snapback rather than following it: Hong Kong's Southbound flow flipped to a net SELL of HK$9.6bn Monday (ending a 4-day buy streak) as the HSI slipped further to 22,383.74; Korea's KOSPI fell another -3.31% to 4,708.54 (its lowest close since Jan 13, a second straight crash day) even as domestic institutions turned net buyers against a 7th-straight foreign sell day; Japan was shut for a holiday, leaving a two-session gap for Tokyo to absorb at its next open.

State-level market-stabilization measures kept escalating rather than winding down: China's margin cut to 80% takes effect Nov 30, Taiwan's short-sale ban is its third intervention in three weeks, and Korea is readying its own stabilization fund -- officials are still treating this as a live threat, not a resolved one.

Macro regime re-stamped to "Mechanical snapback inside an unresolved AI-capex-unwind regime" (riskOnProb 0.38, up from 0.30) -- a modest upgrade for the de-risking having partly abated, but the Fed-odds-up-despite-the-rally and still-wide credit spreads argue against calling this a genuine risk-on turn yet.

regime.label: Mechanical snapback inside an unresolved AI-capex-unwind regime
regime.oneLiner: Monday's Huang-reinstatement-driven rally lifted every index and precious metal in lockstep, but Fed-hike odds rising and credit spreads staying wide say the AI-capex-unwind question hasn't actually been resolved.

topNews.headline: Nvidia board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after reported Trump pressure; stock soars 31%, sparks broadest US rally since April 2025
topNews.actionable: Drove Monday's entire tape, including the silver/miner rebound, but it's a personnel fix, not a resolution of the underlying AI-capex-credibility question -- treat the bounce as fragile rather than confirmed.

topNews.headline: Nvidia SEC accounting-practices probe remains open, unresolved by Huang's reinstatement
topNews.actionable: The Singapore-entity revenue-geography angle flagged last week is still live -- keep watching for MAS/exchange follow-on scrutiny even as the stock price itself has moved on.

topNews.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent warns Fed risks overtightening, breaking with hawkish Fed chorus
topNews.actionable: The dovish counter-voice the market wanted hasn't yet shown up in Fed-funds-futures pricing (Dec-hike odds rose Monday) -- a gap between rhetoric and market pricing worth tracking into the Dec 8-9 FOMC.

topNews.headline: NY Fed's Williams says there's still 'work to do' on inflation, sees 2% goal only by 2028
topNews.actionable: Reinforces why Dec-hike odds rose even as equities rallied -- the Fed speak this week is the opposite of what the levered silver/miner book wants to hear.

topNews.headline: Gold and silver rebound sharply Monday as dollar rally pauses
topNews.actionable: Confirms Friday's metals selloff was margin-liquidation-driven, not a fundamentals shift -- consistent with Shanghai physical premiums and the silver deficit story that predates this week's volatility.
